validated_statements.subject: patients with chronic heart failure
validated_statements.source_text: Several cost-effectiveness analyses consistently found that angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors therapy provides high value for patients with chronic heart failure. A model-based analysis, using generic angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors costs, found angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors therapy was high value.19 Previous analyses also found angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors therapy was high value despite previously higher angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors costs. This includes a trial-based analysis of SOLVD (Studies of Left Ventricular Dysfunction) that modeled long-term outcomes.21 Previous analyses included a range of clinical scenarios including asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction24 and left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction,25 with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors therapy providing high value in each.

validated_statements.subject: Hispanic patients with heart failure
validated_statements.source_text: Despite higher rates of hospitalization for heart failure compared with nonHispanic Whites, Hispanic patients with heart failure have shown lower short-term mortality rates.81 In GWTG, Hispanic patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction had lower mortality (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0..81) than non-Hispanic Whites, but this was not the case for Hispanic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0..43).82 Lower risk of developing atrial fibrillation in the setting of heart failure, compared with White patients.83 Lower mortality rates from heart failure for Asian subgroups when listed as the primary cause of death, compared with non-Hispanic White groups.86 Limited data suggest heart failure mortality rates in American Indians and Alaska Natives are similar to those in White populations.88 delivery of guideline-directed medical therapy and are associated with poorer outcomes.

validated_statements.subject: patients with potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapies
validated_statements.object: quantification of left ventricular ejection fraction
validated_statements.source_text: Pretherapy quantification of left ventricular ejection fraction in patients receiving potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapies serves 4 purposes: 1) pretherapy risk stratification and diagnosis of preexisting cardiomyopathy, 2) establish a reference baseline to which reevaluations can be compared, 3) initiate cardioprotective medications before cancer therapy, and 4) guide choice of cancer therapy. Echocardiography is recommended as the firstline modality for left ventricular ejection fraction assessment given its availability, safety, relatively low cost, and its ability to provide structural and functional information beyond left ventricular ejection fraction.––47 The risk of cancer therapy–related cardiomyopathy varies greatly across cancer therapies and is modified by preexisting cardiovascular risk factors (Table 29).

validated_statements.subject: patients with HFrEF
validated_statements.source_text: In patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and New York Heart Association class II to IV symptoms, an mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone or eplerenone) is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality, if estimated glomerular filtration rate is >30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and serum potassium is <5.0 mEq/L. Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing should be performed at initiation and closely monitored thereafter to minimize risk of hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency

validated_statements.subject: women planning pregnancy
validated_statements.source_text: Pharmacological strategies is Review of all current medications. For women planning pregnancy imminently, modification of heart failure pharmacotherapy including. discontinuation of any angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin (II) receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor or ivabradine medications; within a construct of multidisciplinary shared decision-making, continuation of a beta blocker (most commonly metoprolol), hydralazine, and nitrates; adjustment of diuretic dosing to minimize the risk of placental hypoperfusion.13–15 Ideally, repeat echocardiography approximately 3 mo after preconception heart failure medication adjustments to ensure stability of myocardial structure and function before conception.
